faq.q: What is LLM model quantization?
faq.a: Storing a model's weights, and sometimes its activations, with fewer bits (8 or 4 instead of 16), so it gets smaller and faster for some loss in accuracy.

faq.q: What is the best quantization method for LLMs?
faq.a: It depends on your hardware. On GPUs with FP8 support, 8-bit FP8 is close to lossless. For tight memory, 4-bit weight-only with GPTQ or AWQ is the standard choice, and on a home PC that usually means a Q4_K_M or Q5_K_M GGUF file.

faq.q: When should you quantize a model?
faq.a: When memory, speed or cost is what stops you running it, for example fitting a model on a single consumer GPU or a laptop. If you have plenty of room on all three, quantizing adds risk for little gain.

faq.q: How do I quantize a model?
faq.a: Start from the full-precision model and note its scores, decide what drop you'll accept, pick a method, build a calibration set like your real traffic, quantize with a maintained tool such as llm-compressor or llama.cpp's quantize tool, then compare with the original before you ship.
